objective_for_doctor: A 1-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: expiratory wheezing.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m having significant shortness of breath and expiratory wheezing. I also have a fever and a clear runny nose/nasal congestion.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how old is the child exactly, and when did the wheezing and fever start?  
Doctor: Any history of prior wheezing/asthma, and is there a cough that started around the same time?

She’s 1 year old. The wheezing and shortness of breath started recently (same time as the fever and the clear runny nose/nasal congestion). I don’t know exactly when it started. There’s no mention of any prior wheezing or asthma. I don’t know about a cough.

Doctor: On exam, can I hear wheeze only with exhalation or also at rest, and is there any fast breathing, chest retractions, or low oxygen saturation?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry; Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions); consider REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray if respiratory distress is significant.
At rest and when she exhales, I’ve noticed a wheezing sound when she exhales. I don’t know about fast breathing, chest retractions, or low oxygen saturation.

Doctor: I’m going to check her work of breathing—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry and Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions), and I want to know if she has any fever measured and how high it is.  
Doctor: Also, does she have difficulty feeding, bluish lips, or any vomiting with coughing?

I don’t know if she has difficulty feeding, bluish lips, or vomiting with coughing. 

I have a fever (felt or measured with a thermometer), but I don’t know how high it is.

Doctor: I’ll re-check her respiratory status now—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry and count RR plus look for retractions/stridor; also check and record her measured temperature.  
Doctor: Meanwhile, does she have any signs of dehydration or lethargy, and did this start after a sick contact (family/childcare), or after choking on food?
I don’t know about signs of dehydration or lethargy. I also don’t know if it started after a sick contact (family/childcare) or after choking on food.

Doctor: I’m going to listen to her lungs and evaluate severity—REQUEST TEST: Lung_Auscultation (wheeze pattern), and I need vital signs again: Pulse_Oximetry, RR, and any retractions; also measure temperature.  
Doctor: Has she had poor feeding/less wet diapers, and how is her cough (dry vs productive) or is it mostly wheeze with no cough?
I don’t know about poor feeding or less wet diapers. I also don’t know about her cough (dry vs productive), or whether it’s mostly wheeze with no cough.

Doctor: I’m going to assess severity right now—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry; Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions, ability to feed); Temperature_measurement; and REQUEST TEST: Lung_Auscultation (wheeze vs crackles, focal vs diffuse).  
Doctor: Quick clarifiers for my decision: did she have a new rash, any choking episode/foreign-body concern, and has she improved or worsened since starting—are symptoms steadily worsening?
I don’t know about a new rash. I don’t know about any choking episode/foreign-body concern. I don’t know whether she has improved or worsened since starting.

Doctor: I can’t tell yet how severe this is—please tell me her measured temperature and current SpO₂, and whether she has retractions or faster-than-normal breathing right now.  
Doctor: Also, has the wheeze been continuous since onset, and is there any crackling (not just wheeze) on listening, or does it sound like diffuse expiratory wheeze only?
I don’t know her measured temperature, her current SpO₂, or whether she has retractions or faster-than-normal breathing right now.

Doctor: I can’t make a safe call without severity—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry (SpO₂), Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions/effort), and Temperature_measurement; also perform REQUEST TEST: Lung_Auscultation (note wheeze vs crackles, diffuse vs focal).  
Doctor: One last question: is she drinking/feeding and making wet diapers normally?  
Doctor: If you get results showing diffuse expiratory wheeze after a viral runny nose with no focal crackles, do that pattern fit what you’re seeing—or are there focal signs/marked distress?
I don’t know if she’s drinking/feeding and making wet diapers normally.

Doctor: Thanks—based on what we know (1-year-old with sudden onset fever and clear runny nose/congestion plus expiratory wheeze), I’m most suspicious for **viral bronchiolitis** causing diffuse lower-airway inflammation; I still need severity to guide management.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry; Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions); Temperature_measurement; Lung_Auscultation (diffuse expiratory wheeze vs focal crackles/asymmetry).

I don’t know her measured temperature, her current SpO₂, or whether there are retractions or fast breathing. I also don’t know whether I hear crackles or if the wheeze is diffuse versus focal/asymmetric.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—on exam right now, what are her measured SpO₂ and respiratory rate, and do you see any retractions (or nasal flaring) or is she struggling to feed?  
Doctor: Also, when I listen, is it diffuse expiratory wheeze only, or are there any focal findings/asymmetry or crackles?

I don’t know her measured SpO₂, her respiratory rate, or whether there are retractions (or nasal flaring) or whether she’s struggling to feed. I also don’t know whether the wheeze is diffuse only versus focal/asymmetric, or whether there are crackles.

Doctor: Given we still don’t have severity (SpO₂/RR/retractions) and she’s a 1-year-old with acute expiratory wheeze plus fever and clear runny nose, I’m ordering: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry; Respiratory_Vitals (RR, retractions/nasal flaring); Temperature_measurement; Lung_Auscultation (diffuse vs focal/asymmetric, crackles vs wheeze); and I need to know if she’s taking fluids and making wet diapers.  
Doctor: If her exam shows diffuse expiratory wheeze with viral URI symptoms and no focal crackles/asymmetry, the most likely diagnosis is DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral bronchiolitis (with wheezing)
